category_title: Adolescents who disengage due to perceived teacher indifference and lack of individual support
minimal_context: The student is given a worksheet with repeated problems to complete in a classroom setting.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your next worksheet. It has the same type of problems we did yesterday.

STUDENT: School just became boring. I don’t learn normal, like normal people.

TUTOR: Just keep working on it.

STUDENT: Since I have like learning disabilities, abilities, whatever you wanna call it, I can’t do repeated work.

TUTOR: Please try your best to finish the paper.

STUDENT: I'm just gonna sit here. I just kinda stopped doing it.

options.A: Provide the student with more advanced material, such as sixth-grade level work, instead of the repeated worksheet.
options.B: Adjust the classroom environment to reduce ambient noise and minimize distractions during the repeated worksheet activity.
options.C: Implement systematic instruction and provide frequent, effective feedback, whether praise or corrective, on the repeated worksheet.
options.D: Use behavior-specific praise that includes a description of the behavior, such as praising work on the worksheet.
